subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram channel can be wedged by bad persisted session JSON; status should detect and offer recovery

question: Should bad Telegram-related session-store JSON recovery be limited to read-only status/doctor diagnostics first, or should OpenClaw also add a backed-up reset or automatic quarantine flow?
rationale: Reset and quarantine can restore channel operation but may discard session continuity, so the acceptable recovery behavior needs maintainer state-safety judgment.

options.title: Diagnostics first
options.body: Add shared session-store health checks to status/doctor with backup/reset guidance, leaving destructive recovery to an explicit follow-up.

options.title: Explicit reset command
options.body: Add a user-invoked backed-up reset flow for the affected Telegram/session store once backup path and restart behavior are defined.

options.title: Automatic quarantine
options.body: Move bad session-store artifacts aside on startup/load, accepting a more invasive recovery behavior that needs strong upgrade proof.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics first
recommendation.body: Add shared session-store health checks to status/doctor with backup/reset guidance, leaving destructive recovery to an explicit follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision touches Telegram status UX and channel behavior ownership, where recent history points most strongly to this owner.
